unresolved_must_fix.claim: The revision cuts the sentence placing St. Gaudens in Paris and the paragraph on Adams visiting his studio and going about in his company. P16 then has St. Gaudens take Adams to Amiens with no established contact between them.
unresolved_must_fix.counterevidence: The Sherman statue in the art exhibit hints that the artist is nearby, but this is not stated.

evidence.quote: St. Gaudens himself was in Paris, putting on the work his usual interminable last touches
This summer his health was poor and his spirits were low, but Adams risked going now and then to the studio on Mont Parnasse to draw him out
He could never discuss or dilate on an emotion, or suggest artistic arguments for giving to his work the forms that he felt. His simplicity of thought was excessive.
Once St. Gaudens took him down to Amiens to see the cathedral.

unresolved_must_fix.minimal_repair: Restore one clause after the inarticulateness lines, e.g. 'St. Gaudens himself was in Paris, and sometimes let Adams go about in his company.'
unresolved_must_fix.plan_relation: required: the 'St. Gaudens at Amiens' section presupposes the companionship
unresolved_must_fix.reader_effect: Up to this point the reader has met only the statue in the art exhibit. A personal excursion with its sculptor appears unmotivated, which breaks the scene chain.
unresolved_must_fix.title: Amiens trip lacks St. Gaudens's presence and companionship

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the realization that St. Gaudens on that spot interested Adams more than the cathedral. It also cuts the clause saying Gibbon in fact felt respect for the monument. The text now jumps from the trip straight to the Gibbon quotation.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'perhaps himself' still implies a pose, and 'One sees what one brings' survives.

evidence.quote: did it dawn on Adams's mind that, for his purposes, St. Gaudens on that spot had more interest to him than the cathedral itself
for which he felt in fact the respect which every man of his vast study always feels before objects worthy of it
trying to persuade his readers--perhaps himself--that he was darting a contemptuous look on the stately monument. Without malice

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'St. Gaudens on that spot had more interest… than the cathedral' sentence and the 'for which he felt in fact the respect' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The episode's logic weakens. It is about observers bringing their own era, with St. Gaudens as the specimen. Gibbon's irony also collapses toward a literal contempt.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Amiens pivot and Gibbon's real respect cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'he could see only an absolute fiat in electricity as in faith'. It also cuts the sentences on man translating himself into a new universe with no common scale and entering a supersensual world. Both were kept in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'supersensual, occult' and 'physics stark mad in metaphysics' remain.

evidence.quote: The forces were interchangeable if not reversible, but he could see only an absolute fiat in electricity as in faith.
In these seven years man had translated himself into a new universe which had no common scale of measurement with the old.
the break of continuity amounted to abysmal fracture for a historian's objects. Langley could not help him.
X-rays had played no part whatever in man's consciousness, and the atom itself had figured only as a fiction of thought. Langley seemed prepared for anything

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'absolute fiat… as in faith' sentence and the 'In these seven years… new universe' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essentials: break of continuity; supersensual universe)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The fracture between steam and electricity no longer points toward faith. That weakens the later 'translating rays into faith', and the essential 'supersensual universe' is reduced to an adjective.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Electricity-as-faith fiat and supersensual world removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the chemist objection, i.e. that a chemist would laugh at the process yet could feel the force of both. It also cuts the knife-edge 'two kingdoms of force which had nothing in common but attraction'. The Boston chemist and the Lourdes sentence now follow without their hinge.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'the force of all, though the rays were unborn and the women were dead' partly links the two.

evidence.quote: Such a reversible process would vastly amuse a chemist, but the chemist could not deny that he, or some of his fellow physicists, could feel the force of both.
The knife-edge along which he must crawl, like Sir Lancelot in the twelfth century, divided two kingdoms of force which had nothing in common but attraction.
he would risk translating rays into faith. When Adams was a boy in Boston, the best chemist in the place
The force of the Virgin was still felt at Lourdes, and seemed to be as potent as X-rays

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the chemist sentence and the 'two kingdoms of force… nothing in common but attraction' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: the Boston chemist could feel both)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The Boston chemist reads as a non sequitur, and the turn from rays to Virgin/Venus is abrupt instead of framed as a second kingdom of force.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Bridge from method to the Virgin section dropped

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The plan allows Copernicus/Galileo/Columbus to be compressed to one clause, and the first draft did that. The revision deletes it entirely, leaving 'but the nearest approach' with nothing to be nearer than.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The essential date 310 and the Cross analogy survive.

evidence.quote: Copernicus and Galileo had broken many professorial necks about 1600; Columbus had stood the world on its head towards 1500
Copernicus, Galileo and Columbus had broken many professorial necks
The year 1900 was not the first to upset schoolmasters; but the nearest approach to the revolution of 1900 was that of 310

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the first draft's clause 'Copernicus, Galileo and Columbus had broken many professorial necks'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The scale of comparison that makes 310 the nearest parallel disappears.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Required 1500/1600 comparison removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the ironic 'victory over sex' sentence and the historian's indifference to the moral issue while studying unmoral force. The closer now follows the sexlessness statement directly.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The closer is still intelligible as a quip.

evidence.quote: Society regarded this victory over sex as its greatest triumph, and the historian readily admitted it, since the moral issue, for the moment, did not concern one who was studying the relations of unmoral force.
American art, like the American language and American education, was as far as possible sexless. He cared nothing for the sex of the dynamo until he could measure its energy.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Society regarded this victory over sex…' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: closing line on the dynamo's sex)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The closing joke loses its premise and its irony, so 'cared nothing' reads as an unexplained shift.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Dynamo-sex closer loses its 'unmoral force' setup

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept several self-undercutting cues that the revision removes. These are: the Milky Way contrast, 'an elderly person without other cares', 'Adams, for one, had toiled in vain', the 'German student of 1860', and 'Forty-five years of study… quite futile'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'historical neck broken' and 'Paradise of ignorance' preserve some of the comedy.

evidence.quote: while Adams might as well have stood outside in the night, staring at the Milky Way
Since no one else showed much concern, an elderly person without other cares had no need to betray alarm.
one stumbled as stupidly as though one were still a German student of 1860
for Langley knew what to study, and why, and how. Yet Langley said nothing new
leading at last to the vast forests of scholastic science. In such labyrinths, the staff is a force

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore two short tags: the Milky Way clause and the 'Forty-five years… futile' sentence.
